rules.message: defineConfig sets no default maxDuration; the max-duration page says one must be set, the config page lists it as optional
rules.fix: add a default maxDuration to trigger.config; use timeout.None where unlimited is intended

rules.message: maxDuration is below 5 seconds, the documented minimum
rules.fix: set maxDuration to 5 or more, or timeout.None where no limit is intended

rules.judge: Is critical cleanup (releasing a lock, marking a row, cancelling an external job) only inside cleanup, onSuccess or onFailure, in a task whose maxDuration is short for its work? Those hooks do not run when the run exceeds maxDuration. Answer yes only when the cleanup matters for correctness.
rules.message: critical cleanup lives only in cleanup, onSuccess or onFailure, which are skipped when maxDuration is exceeded
rules.fix: make the cleanup idempotent and also run it where it still executes on timeout

rules.judge: Does a task payload or return value carry bytes by value (Buffer, base64 string, whole file contents), or can an output exceed 10 MB? Answer yes only when the data really travels inside the payload or output, not when it is a reference.
rules.message: a payload or output carries binary or whole-file content by value
rules.fix: pass a reference (URL, storage key, id) and load the bytes inside the task

rules.judge: Is the metadata value a top-level array or string, or does the append run in a loop that can grow without bound? Metadata is an object capped at 256 KB. Answer yes only for those cases; a fixed number of appends is fine.
rules.message: metadata is set to a top-level array or string, or appended in a loop; metadata is an object capped at 256 KB
rules.fix: pass metadata as an object; bound the appended list or store the bulk data elsewhere

rules.judge: Does this child task depend on tags, metadata or limits that only the parent run has, and that are not passed to it explicitly at trigger time? Answer yes only when the child's behaviour changes with the parent's value.
rules.message: child task reads parent-run tags, metadata or limits that it does not receive explicitly
rules.fix: pass them explicitly at trigger time (metadata.current(), ctx.run.tags) instead of relying on inheritance

rules.message: tags array holds more than 10 entries or a tag longer than 128 characters; a run takes 10 tags, each 1 to 128 characters
rules.fix: trim the list to 10 tags and shorten any tag over 128 characters

rules.message: debounce is set without maxDelay, so repeated triggers can push the run back indefinitely (an error when triggered with triggerAndWait); or delay equals maxDelay, which leaves no room to debounce
creates a client (createClient, Pool, Kafka or MongoClient) and this file registers no error listener
rules.fix: register an error listener on the client
rules.judge: Confirm the client is created inside task code and is long-lived (module scope or reused across attempts). A client created and closed inside one request handler is fine; one created in a task without an error listener can crash the run with TASK_RUN_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION.

rules.message: calls NestFactory.createApplicationContext in a file that imports @trigger.dev/
rules.fix: use the service directly inside the task instead of booting a Nest application context

rules.message: this task id literal is also declared by another task in the project
rules.fix: give each task a unique id

rules.message: trigger.config dirs does not cover the folder that holds a task, or lists a folder that does not exist
rules.fix: fix dirs so every task folder is listed and exists

rules.message: runs.list is called inside a loop
rules.fix: replace polling with idempotency keys, waits or realtime subscriptions

rules.judge: Does this task process large in-memory data (big files, large arrays, image, video or model work) on the default machine, with no retry.outOfMemory configured? Answer yes only when the memory need can plausibly exceed the default machine.
rules.message: task processes large in-memory data with no outOfMemory retry configured
rules.fix: choose a larger machine preset or add an OOM retry through retry.outOfMemory

rules.judge: Does this task open a stream (.pipe(), .append() or .writer()) and then wait for an hour or more (wait.for or wait.until) without writing to the stream in between? Answer yes only for that sequence.
rules.message: a stream is opened and then the task waits an hour or more with no writes in between
rules.fix: close the stream before the long wait, or write heartbeat chunks during it
